text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.3% today to $134.47, extending a sharp two-week decline of 11%. The core driver appears to be weakening oil prices: US crude dropped to $99.64 per barrel today, well below the $107+ range seen earlier this week, which directly pressures the margins and cash flow of an oil major. This came after the company reported quarterly earnings on November 5th, suggesting investors may have digested results and are now reacting to deteriorating commodity prices.

The broader context amplifies this headwind. Midterm election results have strengthened renewable energy policy momentum at a time when geopolitical tensions—including stalled Iran negotiations—have failed to sustain oil prices. Oil majors like ConocoPhillips face a structural shift: energy markets are pricing in both softer near-term demand and longer-term energy transition risks, leaving little support for the stock even as geopolitical risks linger unresolved.
